metadata.title: Toronto dbt companies and people for the Toronto dbt Meetup
metadata.purpose: Find Toronto companies using dbt, and people who could speak at or attend the Toronto dbt Meetup.
method: v1 (2026-09-24): one budgeted research sub-agent (~18 web searches: dbt Summit/Coalesce/World Tour agendas filtered to local employers, company blogs, local data meetups and user groups, women-in-data communities sourced through their own events) plus a logged-out LinkedIn Jobs scan (keywords=dbt, up to 150 ads checked for the whole word 'dbt'). Past chapter speakers added from enriched/toronto-dbt-meetup.json. Same merge and scoring rules as berlin_planning/SEARCH_METHOD.md §1 Step 6 (strict tier 1: local or unknown location + a dbt item from 2024 onwards; emerging voices raised).

Lesson: For mid-sized chapters, the local Snowflake and Databricks user groups (Bevy pages at usergroups.snowflake.com / usergroups.databricks.com) give the best 2025-26 local speaker lists and organisers, and they fetch cleanly with web_fetch.
Lesson: Dormant or rebranded 'Modern Data Stack' meetups (TMDS here) hold the city's historic dbt speaker pool. Pull them with Meetup gql2 and re-verify current roles.
Lesson: Matching Toronto employer names against the dbt Summit speaker page's text quickly finds local conference speakers. Coalesce 2025's Cvent pages need a browser.

v2 (2026-10-01): v2 extension (2026-10-01): ~20 web searches (exhausted the shared budget early) plus direct fetches: Meetup gql2 past events for 25 Toronto/Waterloo groups found via gql2 groupSearch (Snowflake, Airflow, Kafka, TDPC, PyLadies, R-Ladies, AWS Women in Tech Ontario, ClickHouse, PyData and others), Medium publication feeds via rss2json (Loblaw Digital, Shopify Data, Wealthsimple, Faire), the Databricks Data + AI World Tour Toronto 2025 catalog, the Toronto Generative AI Summit speaker page, the dbt Summit 2026 speaker JSON, dev.to and GitHub user search by location. Added 38 people; same scoring rules as berlin_planning/SEARCH_METHOD.md section 1 Step 6.
Lesson: Meetup gql2 works from plain curl (no browser), and groupSearch with lat/lon finds the city's data groups in one call.
Lesson: Medium blocks curl and WebFetch with Cloudflare; api.rss2json.com returns a publication's last 10 posts with full text, but rate-limits after about 10 new feeds.
Lesson: Loblaw Digital's Medium is the best Toronto company blog for dbt authors; Shopify's data posts are 2020-era and Faire's are AI/ML.
Lesson: dev.to and GitHub location search yield job-seeker portfolios rather than speakers, so they are not worth the calls.
Lesson: Databricks World Tour and AI-summit agendas give senior bank and insurer leaders, who suit panels better than technical talks.

v2 (2026-10-01): location pass. 6 people placed from public pages (Meetup hosts and RSVPs, GitHub, speaker bios, author boxes, recent in-person talks at a local-office employer) and LinkedIn search results (0 of them),, or from the same person's located record in another chapter's file, by the evidence rules in research/README.md. Each placed person has a 'location (high|medium)' note and evidence link. 5 people are still unknown.

v3 (2026-10-01): women-in-data pass with fetches only (no web search, about 18 fetches): Meetup gql2 groupSearch near Toronto with 16 queries, then the past events of Toronto WiMLDS, Women in Big Data Toronto, AWS User Group Women in Tech Ontario, PyLadies Toronto, R-Ladies Toronto, QueerTech Toronto, Beyond Networking (Women Techmakers) and a new Women in STEM/Finance group; the Women Techmakers Luma page; the GDG Toronto and GDG Cloud Toronto events APIs and 4 event pages; the WiDS Toronto event page and a WiDS round-up. 7 people added (1 speaker, 6 organisers as connectors). Nobody's gender is recorded or inferred.

Lesson: Women Techmakers Ambassadors in Toronto post on a small Meetup group named 'Beyond Networking - Women in Tech' (urlname north-york-wisdom-business-network-meetup-group) and register on Luma. The Luma page names the hosts.
Lesson: GDG Toronto (chapter 959) and GDG Cloud Toronto (chapter 259) IWD pages name organisers only, not panellists.
Lesson: AWS User Group Women in Tech Ontario runs online talks; its May 2026 talk was the only data engineering talk at a Toronto women-in-tech group since 2024.

v4 (2026-10-01): company pass: HN Who is hiring via Algolia (6 queries), Greenhouse/Lever/Ashby boards for 43 Toronto employers, the getdbt.com case-study sitemap, GitHub code and repo search for 13 local orgs, and Meetup gql2 for 7 Toronto data groups.

v4 (2026-10-01): 13 LinkedIn profiles taken from pages already tied to each person (event, speaker and author pages, GitHub social accounts) with research/harvest_linkedin.py, without searching. Page links are medium confidence, GitHub links high.

v5 (2026-10-05): second people pass: about 30 web calls, one at a time, for people not yet on file (first-time speakers, speakers at other local events, women-in-data communities, connectors); every link checked before merging.
Generic web searches for Toronto dbt authors returned mostly job ads and national dbt pages, with no new local author.
Bevy pages for the Snowflake and Databricks Toronto user groups fetch cleanly, but name organisers only. Speakers come from the individual event pages.
Medium rss2json feeds returned HTTP 500 for guessed publication slugs, and the dbt tag feed shows no location, so it cannot place authors in Toronto.
Speaker bios on getdbt.com and Coalesce pages state a city, which is the quickest way to place a vendor-employed speaker.

v6 (2026-10-05): people pass with research/find_local_speakers.py: speakers and hosts of local data groups (meetup speakerDetails, bevy chapters) and github data people with a town in the region; speakers kept only when a linkedin lookup placed them in the region.
Lesson: the in-person flag on meetup and bevy events does not show where a speaker lives; many listed speakers live elsewhere, so a speaker needs a location lookup before counting as local.
v7 (2026-10-06): github pass with the faster find_local_speakers.py: data people with a town in the region.

field_definitions.metadata.region: the meetup chapter this dataset serves
field_definitions.metadata.schema_version: shared schema version used by every <region>_dbt_companies.json file (see research/README.md §4)
field_definitions.companies.type: employer | consultancy | vendor | outsourcing | recruiter | community | independent | other
field_definitions.companies.watchlist: true for companies checked but not yet showing in-region dbt work (unconfirmed local presence, or weak/none dbt signal); kept so they are not re-researched
field_definitions.companies.excluded_from_outreach: true for companies deliberately not approached (e.g. dbt Labs staff who already speak regularly)
field_definitions.companies.local_presence: confirmed | not_confirmed | none — whether the company has people/roles in the region
field_definitions.companies.dbt_signal: strong = public post/case study/talk, or dbt required / core stack in a job ad; medium = dbt listed among alternatives, tagged by a job board's skill extraction, or seen only in a snippet; nice-to-have = listed as a plus; weak = unverified; none = stack appears to be non-dbt, or not applicable
field_definitions.companies.other_evidence.type: article | talk | case_study | oss | job_posting | careers | company_blog | conference_talk | meetup | podcast | news | profile | blog_scanned (blog checked, even if nothing relevant) | other
field_definitions.companies.job_postings.dbt_mentioned_in_: true = dbt seen in the ad text (or tagged from the text by the job board); null = only seen in a search snippet about the ad
field_definitions.companies.job_postings.posted_date: date shown on the job board (YYYY-MM-DD), null if unknown
field_definitions.companies.job_postings.last_seen: last run in which the ad was still listed
field_definitions.companies.job_postings.job_family / work: as labelled by the job board (e.g. Analytics Engineer; Remote/Hybrid/On-site); null if not labelled
field_definitions.companies.people.id: kebab-case ASCII name, stable across runs
field_definitions.companies.people.city / based_in_region: city as seen publicly; based_in_region true = evidence they are in the region, false = evidence elsewhere, null = unverified
field_definitions.companies.people.level: leadership if the title contains Head/Director/VP/Chief/Founder/C-level/Manager/Lead, otherwise working
field_definitions.companies.people.confidence: High = name + title + company visible in a public source; Medium = indirect evidence; Low = weak evidence
field_definitions.companies.people.linkedin_confidence: high = name + company/role in the search result title; medium = indirect or name variant; low = searched, not found; not_searched
field_definitions.companies.people.profile_urls: other public professional profiles, as [{type, url, source}]; meetup, x and bluesky profiles can take a message, the others show the person's work: type is one of github, meetup, zenn, qiita, velog, medium, devto, substack, ithome, sessionize, x, bluesky, website, note; source is the page that ties the profile to the person. never an email address or phone number
field_definitions.companies.people.mentions_dbt: true if any of the person's public content (or profile snippet) mentions dbt; false if content found without dbt; null if unknown
field_definitions.companies.people.meetup_fit.speaker_pote: high = has given a dbt talk, 2+ public talks, spoke at this chapter before, or priority_tier 1; medium = some public content; low = none found
field_definitions.companies.people.meetup_fit.attendee_pot: high = in region and public dbt content (or confirmed practitioner at a strong-dbt company); medium = in-region/unknown data practitioner; low = outside the region or weak identification
field_definitions.companies.people.internal_vinted: true for Vinted colleagues (kept for completeness, not outreach targets)
field_definitions.companies.people.priority_tier: 1 = strong recent lead: a proven speaker with a relevant recent talk, or an emerging_voice in (or not known to be outside) the region with authored content from 2024 onwards; 2 = good lead / needs verification / older content / relevant talk at another meetup; 3 = peripheral, off-topic or remote; organiser / backup / connector = special roles
field_definitions.companies.people.past_chapter_talks: talks this person gave at this chapter's own meetups, matched by name
field_definitions.companies.people.speaker_evidence.type: talk | panel | podcast | article | case_study | oss | interview | organiser | host | post | profile
field_definitions.companies.people.speaker_evidence.topics: 1-3 topics, most relevant first, only from metadata.topic_vocabulary (pipeline/enrich.py::TOPIC_VOCABULARY); organiser/host/profile entries are tagged 'community'
field_definitions.companies.people.speaker_evidence.conten: stable id; an item with several authors appears under each of them with the same content_id
field_definitions.companies.people.speaker_evidence.url_pr: direct = the item itself; overview_page = a listing/homepage where the item appears
field_definitions.past_meetups.talks.topics: 1-3 topics, most relevant first, only from metadata.topic_vocabulary (pipeline/enrich.py::TOPIC_VOCABULARY); organiser/host/profile entries are tagged 'community'
field_definitions.companies.people.lead_type: proven_speaker = has given a talk, panel or podcast, or spoke at this chapter; emerging_voice = has authored public content (blog post, article, newsletter, open-source project, LinkedIn post) but no talk found yet — a priority for first-time speaker invitations; featured = only quoted or profiled in someone else's content (case study, interview, team feature); no_public_content = none found
field_definitions.companies.people.pronouns: pronouns exactly as the person publishes them (e.g. on a speaker listing, bio or profile headline); null when not self-stated. Never inferred from names, photos or third-person wording
field_definitions.companies.people.sourced_via: channels through which the person was found (list): company_blog_scan | case_study | conference_or_meetup_agenda | data_berlin_meetup | women_in_data_community | chapter_meetup_history | newsletter_or_blog | podcast | github | linkedin_search | job_ad_company_search | other

caveats: Titles, employers and cities come from public pages/snippets and are often inferred from the employer's HQ — verify before outreach.
Only public professional information is recorded; no personal contact details. Pronouns only when self-stated.
Titles, employers and cities come from public event pages and blog bylines, some from 2023; verify current role before outreach.
Loblaw Digital co-authors' titles were not stated in the posts.
Several Meetup event pages link speakers' LinkedIn profiles; these were not recorded because they did not come from a search result.

LinkedIn: 3 of 69 people have a profile url, taken word for word from search results. 66 were never searched (linkedin_confidence 'not_searched'); the 2026-10-01 pass searched the best-ranked leads with no known location first.
Speakers from women-in-data community events are recorded by where they spoke (sourced_via women_in_data_community). No one's gender is recorded or inferred.
Titles, employers and cities come from public pages and search snippets. Verify before outreach.
Michelle Ark's Coalesce talk title, year and abstract were not visible, because the speaker page now redirects to the dbt Summit page. Toronto comes from a search-result snippet of her speaker bio.
Kishawna Peck's current city and the date of the latest conference were not confirmed. The Toronto Womxn in Data Science speaker pages on amii.ca returned 404.
About 25 calls were used and the run found few new people. Toronto looks close to exhausted for open web sources.
